title: get
summary: Find a saved command, copy it, show it, or run it. Also searches shell history.
notes: With a name, `get` copies the command to the clipboard. With no name it lists commands and asks you to pick one.
`-x` runs the command. With the shell wrapper from `cwm setup` it runs in your current shell, and the exit code of the command is passed through.
`--show` prints only the command on stdout. Tables, prompts and errors go to stderr, so it is safe to pipe.
Placeholders written as `%name%` or `{{name}}` are filled in by prompts. Comment lines are ignored.
`-f` turns on fuzzy matching: the letters you type must appear in order, not next to each other.
History search (`-h`) reads your shell history file. `-a` reads what `cwm watch` recorded for the current folder.

flags.name: -x, --exec
flags.desc: Run the command instead of copying it.

flags.name: --show
flags.desc: Print the command without copying it.

flags.name: -l, --list
flags.desc: List commands without asking for a choice.

flags.name: -f, --fuzzy
flags.desc: Fuzzy search saved commands or history.

flags.name: -a, --active
flags.desc: Search commands recorded in the current project folder.

flags.name: -c, --copy
flags.desc: Read from the copy bank database.

flags.name: -n, --count <n>
flags.desc: Limit the number of results. History default is 10.
